articles.title: Como está a economia da Argentina? Crescimento e queda da inflação contrastam com pobreza e desemprego | G1
articles.standfirst: Setores ligados às exportações puxam a atividade, enquanto consumo, indústria e investimentos perdem força. Número de empregadores com funcionários registrados caiu 6,3% desde novembro de 2023.
articles.summary: Setores ligados às exportações puxam a atividade, enquanto consumo, indústria e investimentos perdem força. Número de empregadores com funcionários registrados caiu 6,3% desde nove
articles.body:
O presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, faz um discurso especial durante a 55ª reunião anual do Fórum Econômico Mundial em Davos, Suíça, em 23 de janeiro de 2025. — Foto: Reuters

A economia da Argentina virou tema do primeiro debate presidencial para o segundo turno das eleições brasileiras.

Ao questionar candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) sobre sua proximidade com Javier Milei , o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) perguntou se o adversário pretendia reproduzir no Brasil a política econômica adotada pelo argentino.

A discussão ocorreu depois de Daniella Marques, coordenadora econômica da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro, apontar o governo de Milei como inspiração para medidas de redução de impostos e burocracia.

Os indicadores, porém, revelam um quadro mais complexo: a economia argentina voltou a crescer e a inflação desacelerou, mas a pobreza e o desemprego aumentaram , enquanto o consumo interno e setores importantes para a geração de empregos enfrentam dificuldades.

Economia cresce nos dois primeiros trimestres de 2026

O Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) argentino cresceu 2,3% no primeiro trimestre de 2026 em comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior. No segundo trimestre, a alta foi de 2% na mesma base de comparação, segundo o Instituto Nacional de Estatística e Censos (Indec).

Os resultados positivos, porém, escondem uma perda de ritmo. Entre abril e junho, o PIB caiu 0,6% em relação aos três primeiros meses do ano, já descontados os efeitos sazonais. O consumo privado recuou 2,4%, o consumo público diminuiu 2,3% e os investimentos caíram 0,8%.

Na comparação anual, a formação bruta de capital fixo — indicador dos investimentos realizados na economia — teve queda de 11,1%.

A composição do crescimento também ajuda a entender esse cenário.

No primeiro trimestre, agropecuária, pesca, mineração e intermediação financeira estiveram entre os principais motores da expansão, enquanto a indústria de transformação recuou 1,7% e o comércio varejista caiu 0,3%.

No segundo trimestre, atividades ligadas às exportações voltaram a se destacar: a pesca cresceu 44,7%, a mineração e a extração em pedreiras avançaram 16,4%, e a agropecuária teve alta de 6,9%.

As exportações de bens e serviços aumentaram 13,7%, enquanto as importações diminuíram 8,6%. Em sentido contrário, a indústria manufatureira recuou 2,1%.

➡️ Os números apontam para uma recuperação desigual. Enquanto atividades ligadas às exportações avançam, segmentos mais dependentes do mercado interno enfrentam dificuldades.

Um dos principais resultados reivindicados pelo governo de Javier Milei é a desaceleração da inflação. O índice oficial de preços, que chegou a quase 290% no acumulado de 12 meses, caiu para cerca de 30% durante os primeiros dois anos de sua gestão.

Em agosto de 2026, a inflação mensal desacelerou para 1,7%, o menor resultado desde junho de 2025. A estabilização dos preços foi acompanhada de um forte ajuste fiscal, com cortes de gastos públicos, retirada de subsídios e outras medidas de austeridade.

A redução da inflação foi inicialmente acompanhada de uma queda da pobreza, que havia atingido 52,9% em 2024. Em 2026, porém, essa melhora perdeu força. A proporção de argentinos abaixo da linha da pobreza passou de 28,2% no segundo semestre de 2025 para 32,3% no primeiro semestre deste ano .

O levantamento do Indec abrange 31 aglomerados urbanos e indica que 9,7 milhões de pessoas viviam na pobreza. Foi a primeira alta do indicador em dois anos.

A extrema pobreza também aumentou. O número de pessoas nessa situação passou de 1,9 milhão, equivalente a 6,3% da população pesquisada, para 2,2 milhões, ou 7,5%.

Pelo critério do Indec, são consideradas indigentes as pessoas cuja renda não é suficiente para comprar uma cesta de alimentos capaz de suprir as necessidades diárias de energia e proteína.

Desemprego e informalidade pressionam trabalhadores

O mercado de trabalho também mostra os limites da recuperação. A taxa de desemprego chegou a 7,9% no segundo trimestre de 2026, ante 7,6% no mesmo período de 2025, segundo o Indec.

A estimativa é que aproximadamente 1,8 milhão de argentinos estivessem desempregadas nos 31 aglomerados urbanos acompanhados pelo instituto.

Além disso, quase metade da população economicamente ativa trabalha na informalidade, sem vínculo formal de emprego.

O quadro combina, portanto, uma inflação muito menor do que a registrada no início do governo Milei com dificuldades para transformar a estabilização econômica em melhora contínua das condições de vida.

Empresas e indústria enfrentam dificuldades

A pressão sobre a atividade doméstica também aparece nos dados sobre empregadores com trabalhadores registrados.

Segundo a Superintendência de Riscos do Trabalho (SRT), o número de empregadores com pelo menos um funcionário registrado no sistema de seguro contra acidentes caiu de 512.357, em novembro de 2023, para 480.067, em julho de 2026.

Foram 32.290 empregadores a menos , uma redução de 6,3%. A queda marcou o 18º mês consecutivo de retração.

➡️ O indicador, porém, exige cautela: deixar de aparecer no cadastro não significa necessariamente que uma empresa tenha fechado definitivamente . Um empregador também pode sair da base por ficar sem funcionários registrados, passar por uma reorganização ou sofrer alguma alteração cadastral.

Ainda assim, entidades empresariais apontam que o consumo enfraquecido, os custos de energia e as condições de financiamento pressionam especialmente as pequenas e médias empresas.

A maior abertura às importações acrescentou outra fonte de pressão sobre a produção local. Segundo o Centro de Economia Política Argentina (CEPA), as compras externas de bens de consumo cresceram 34,7% no primeiro semestre de 2026 em relação ao mesmo período de 2023. No mesmo intervalo, a produção industrial argentina caiu 12%.

Dados da União Industrial Argentina e da Confederação Argentina da Média Empresa também indicam que os custos elevados e o endividamento das famílias têm limitado o consumo e o desempenho das empresas locais.

articles.title: Buy these 2 stocks amid AI financing concerns: Analyst
articles.summary: Investing.com -- The withdrawal of the Firmus IPO has raised some concerns, but Truist analysts believe it is only a matter of time the quality of the digita...
articles.body:
Investing.com -- The withdrawal of the Firmus IPO has raised some concerns, but Truist analysts believe it is only a matter of time the quality of the digital platforms and IT services space becomes clear. In their recent note, firm analysts identify two cloud providers with backlogs providing meaningful revenue visibility, and say the softness in their shares is a buying opportunity.

Amid recent AI financing concerns, Truist recommends buying CoreWeave Inc (NASDAQ:CRWV) and Nebius Group NV (NASDAQ:NBIS) shares.

Truist has Buy ratings on both names and a price target of $165 on CRWV stock and $355 on NBIS.

Firm analysts say their multiple assumption for CRWV represents a premium to the median of 21x 2027 EV/EBIT among AI cloud providers and leading providers of AI infrastructure.

Meanwhile, NBIS' 4.5x 2028E EV/Sales multiple on their 2028E revenue estimate is above the peer average in the AI cloud and hyperscaler industry. Truist notes that the premium is warranted given the expectation that NBIS will deliver industry-leading growth rates across 2026E-2028E.

The research firm observes that over the next two years, the AI cloud/neocloud cohort could report strong revenue growth rates given the compute shortage. However, the firm believes that cloud providers that demonstrate the necessary execution, financing, and upstack expansion to build sustainable businesses will distinguish themselves in the coming quarters.

"We continue to see CRWV and NBIS as leaders in the space, with their status as the only two companies holding Platinum rankings on SemiAnalysis's ClusterMax 3.0 providing a further proof point of the quality of their platforms," the analysts said.

To illustrate the difference in scale between Firmus, which has an active capacity of 46MW, on one hand, and CRWV and NBIS on the other, the analysts note CRWV has 1.5GW (1,500MW) and NBIS has ~450MW of active capacity. CRWV's addition of 500MW capacity in Q2 is equivalent to ~10x the total capacity each company has brought online in their corporate history.

Truist emphasises that these numbers represent the actual capacity that AI clouds will be able to recognise revenue on. Furthermore, companies with larger backlogs and limited active capacity will face a higher execution hurdle if they must catch up and generate revenue.

articles.title: Option Traders Brace for Volatility Surge as AI Jitters Jolt Market
articles.summary: Accelerating US inflation and tremors across the AI sector jolted stocks in recent days, and some investors are now betting that bigger swings in tech shares...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Accelerating US inflation and tremors across the AI sector jolted stocks in recent days, and some investors are now betting that bigger swings in tech shares will finally spread to the broader market.

Before Wednesday, the S&P 500 Index had gone 53 sessions without a 1% drop, the longest stretch since January 2020. It's not just that volatility was low, it had also been remarkably stable.

For many traders, it's becoming more a question of when rather than if the current equity rotations spill over into broader liquidation, causing volatility to spike. Despite the calm indexes, elevated Treasury yields have contributed to pockets of higher volatility among artificial-intelligence infrastructure companies and other adjacent sectors. On a macro level, persistent fuel and food inflation, driven by wars in Iran and Ukraine that show little signs of ending, adds pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates.

"The macro environment remains quite fragile," said Jeremy Wien, managing partner at Moo Point Capital Management. "The VIX was not pricing in nearly as much risk as I believe it should be at the moment, mostly because the SPX hasn't until Friday moved in a manner that seems to warrant it."

While Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX, call options looked like a bargain for much of the year, the minuscule swings in VIX futures paint a different picture — one where it looks expensive to hold call options betting on a spike in volatility. The vol of vol — measured with the Cboe VIX of VIX Index known as VVIX — had been sitting around the weakest level of the past two years before jumping on Friday.

Still, that hasn't deterred some investors from building long volatility positions.

Bank of America Corp. strategists recently wrote that VIX call positioning by customers has risen sharply and is approaching the levels of summer 2024, highlighting general demand for forward volatility.

One knock-on effect of customers owning the VIX calls is the potential for a volatility gamma squeeze if option dealers who are short the calls need to buy futures to re-hedge their positions. That could exacerbate a sudden VIX surge as appeared to happen on Friday, when the 6-point intraday increase in the volatility gauge exceeded the expected reaction to a nearly 1.5% drop in the S&P 500.

articles.title: Intel (INTC) Lands A Major Customer For Its 14A Foundry Process
articles.summary: Intel (NasdaqGS: INTC) said Tesla has agreed to use its upcoming 14A manufacturing process as a foundry customer. The chipmaker reported progress on output f...
articles.body:
Intel (NasdaqGS: INTC) said Tesla has agreed to use its upcoming 14A manufacturing process as a foundry customer.

The chipmaker reported progress on output from its 18A node, highlighting current production results for the advanced manufacturing technology.

Intel announced a US$20b equity raise earmarked for new factory buildouts tied to its foundry expansion plans.

The Tesla 14A deal, 18A progress and US$20b raise only capture part of what is changing for Intel today. We have also flagged 1 other big win for Intel.

Consider reviewing other chip and equipment stocks connected to the build out of AI compute and networking capacity through 55 AI infrastructure stocks .

Intel operates one of the few globally scaled chip fabrication networks, and this combination of foundries, design work and related services gives it a direct role in supplying high performance computing hardware to large customers that want more capacity and vendor diversity.

How does Tesla using Intel's 14A process change the foundry story?

Tesla showing up as a 14A customer gives Intel something it has needed for its foundry push, a high profile external client willing to bet on its leading edge roadmap. It signals chip buyers are at least willing to test Intel as an alternative manufacturing partner for advanced logic, not just legacy nodes.

Does this update reshape the existing Intel Narrative investors have been using?

The Tesla agreement and 18A output update line up closely with the Narrative's key catalyst that heavy CapEx on 18A, 14A and advanced packaging must translate into real foundry demand. At the same time, the US$20b equity raise highlights the Narrative risk that aggressive spending could weigh on free cash flow and stretch the path to foundry breakeven.

See how these catalysts shape Intel's path to a $116 fair value .

What is the clearest next sign that this Intel news is paying off?

The most concrete marker will be whether Intel starts disclosing additional named 14A or 18A foundry customers and meaningful dollar commitments as it funds new fabs with the US$20b raise. Investors can also watch for future updates on Intel Foundry operating losses to see if the segment moves closer to management's late 2028 breakeven goal.

articles.title: No agenda, no rush, no leaving San Francisco: Benchmark’s partners on investing in a frenzied market
articles.summary: Benchmark may have grown its funds and swapped out some partners, but onstage the five who are left sounded like friends who just happen to be running one of...
articles.body:
The players sometimes change. I sat down with four of Benchmark's partners three years ago , and three of those individuals are no longer with the firm. The capital commitments have changed, too. This summer, Benchmark announced $2 billion across two funds, marking only the second time in its 31-year history that it has veered from raising a far smaller vehicle.

But at this week's TechCrunch Disrupt, the venture firm's five partners convincingly portrayed a close-knit team that's not about to put the pedal to the metal, even as many of their rivals do exactly that. The world may be speeding up, but they're investing at the pace Benchmark always has: just two or three new bets per year per partner. The world is drowning in information, yet their Monday partner meetings still have no agenda. And while economic indicators point to trouble ahead, they don't seem too bothered, seeing many of the warning signs as products of X-fueled hysteria.

Here's what Benchmark's five general partners — gathered together on our stage — had to say at the show. Some of the comments below have been edited for length and clarity; you can watch the full interview at the end of the article.

Benchmark has evolved in some ways, including a bigger core fund and a new growth fund. How do you think about adapting without losing what makes you Benchmark?

Peter Fenton: The craft that hasn't changed is the core fund: working closely with founders at the beginning. It's usually a 10-to-15-year commitment, [working] shoulder to shoulder, and that doesn't scale. There's also been inflation. We held the core fund at $500 million for 20 years, and it has just inflated to be consistent with the existing economy, which we hadn't done and that was probably a tactical error on our part.

[As for the growth fund] it's an expansion of our mandate. In some ways, we get permission from the ecosystem to do more than just the core early-stage business. [Not having this previously] was a fork in our eye. A number of opportunities that came to Benchmark would have returned somewhere between 10 and 1,000x to Benchmark, and we were constricted by our early-stage focus.

Are you thinking to make handful of bets with that $1.25 billion growth fund?

Fenton: We all have different answers, which is the beauty of a partnership. I'd love for us to have, as that great J.P. Morgan paper puts it, the agony and ecstasy of a concentrated portfolio. If the fund is successful, one or two investments will generate 90% of the returns. So I think it's four to six, maybe seven to eight.

articles.title: PFRDA readies plan to onboard gig workers on National Pension System
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lakhs of gig and platform workers may soon be able to plan for their retirement savings as Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lakhs of gig and platform workers may soon be able to plan for their retirement savings as Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is working to open National Pension System (NPS) accounts for workers who are part of the e-shram database.“Under the social security code, govt has to provide social security benefits to gig and platform workers. For the pension benefit, PFRDA suggested using the e-shramik model. We are tying up with the e-shram database now, will get a consent from the gig workers and open NPS accounts for them,” chairman S Raman told TOI in an interview.These new accounts will be opened using the recently launched NPS Tatkal option, which allows subscribers to open accounts digitally and instantly through UPI-linked payment platforms, without requiring any paperwork.The e-shramik model, which was launched in Oct 2025, enables both workers and aggregators to make flexible and micro-contributions -- as low as Rs 99 -- to the account without rigid monthly mandates. It is also linked to a Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) so that a worker can access it anytime, irrespective of his or her employment or platform affiliation.Utilising the e-shramik model is important as platforms have not been very forthcoming over the share and nature of contributions to be made by them towards social security benefits of workers. This provides them with a flexible option. For the gig and platform workers, this is beneficial as it allows them -- without regular earnings -- to start saving for retirement instead of deferring it.“By default, these new accounts will follow the investment pattern of NPS Sanchaya. Afterwards, if the subscriber is interested to change their investment allocations, they will have the option to do so. This will allow them steady returns and build their savings over time,” said Raman.NPS Sanchay follows a pre-defined, conservative-to-moderate investment pattern similar to govt sector NPS schemes. This is in contrast to regular NPS, where subscribers must actively choose the mix of investment between equities, corporate bonds, govt securities, and alternate assets.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nilekani-backed Fundamentum AI fund raises 3,000 crore
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Nandan Nilekani-backed Fundamentum’s third fund has secured Rs 3,000 crore from investors and raised its fundraising ceiling to Rs 3,500 crore
articles.body: BENGALURU: Nandan Nilekani-backed Fundamentum’s third fund has secured Rs 3,000 crore from investors and raised its fundraising ceiling to Rs 3,500 crore following strong demand, as the venture capital firm prepares to make larger bets on Indian artificial intelligence and deep-tech startups.The fund, managed by Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A), is led by Fundamentum co-founder Ashish Kumar. In an interview with TOI, Kumar said the firm had closed fundraising at Rs 3,000 crore and was negotiating with institutional investors to raise another Rs 500 crore.It expects to complete the final close within the next two months. About 70% of the capital has come from Indian investors, largely family offices, while overseas investors account for the remaining 30%. — Supriya RoyYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Amid UPI user surge, Visa bets on affluent consumers
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Visa, the world’s largest payments network, is expanding its focus in India towards affluent consumers, cross-border spending and higher-value
articles.body: MUMBAI: Visa, the world’s largest payments network, is expanding its focus in India towards affluent consumers, cross-border spending and higher-value payment services as UPI dominates everyday transactions such as groceries. The payment company is also expanding beyond interchange fees into B2B fund transfers, data consulting, cyber-resilience and AI-enabled threat detection.Visa group country manager Suresh Sethi said there is a segmentation in the digital payments market, where UPI is being used increasingly for day-to-day low-value payments while credit cards are used for other aspects of life. “We naturally also segment our markets. For us, what becomes very important is one, the entire affluent segment which is expanding as more people move from the mass-affluent segment into the affluent category,” said Sethi. The rise in overseas travel is creating another opportunity for card payments. “When you look at cross-border travel, Visa does bring the capability of global acceptance. You can virtually carry one single card with you when you’re travelling globally,” he said.Competition in premium cards is also shifting beyond traditional benefits such as airport lounge access. Foreign-exchange pricing and curated privileges are becoming more important, with zero-FX products allowing overseas transactions at the bank-rate conversion without a markup. Sethi said dynamic currency conversion has also encouraged consumers to use cards instead of prepaid forex instruments. Visa has expanded premium offerings including Infinite Privilege and Infinite Reserve.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: PNB ventures to win back young customers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: From facilitating loans to startups to special savings accounts for students and credit card offers, state-run Punjab National Bank (PNB) is
articles.body: NEW DELHI: From facilitating loans to startups to special savings accounts for students and credit card offers, state-run Punjab National Bank (PNB) is rolling out the red carpet for young customers.“Every young person wants to hold a credit card today, so our effort is to fulfil that. Second, we are easing the loan approval process for them, particularly for startups where they can avail credit digitally without getting involved in paperwork. We have also come up with a special savings scheme for them. Efforts are underway to get in touch with educational institutions, so that we can tap into the young age cohort,” PNB managing director and CEO Ashok Chandra told TOI.The move is part of an exercise to win back customers who have flocked to more nimble private banks in recent years, backed by better technology and a suite of products, often peddled by intrusive relationship managers. Recently, finance minister FM Nirmala Sitharaman had exhorted state-run banks to adopt a “lifecycle” approach and aim to become the preferred financial partner, from campus to career and beyond.Having reported a 13% rise in net profit to Rs 5,532 crore in the Sept quarter, Chandra is hopeful of the momentum sustaining with deposit and credit growth being on track in the current financial year, with no pressure to increase the deposit rates, at least for the time being.Besides, Chandra said El Nino had so far not impacted the bank’s loan book as it had seen sustained demand in its strongholds of north and north-western India, though he is keeping a close watch. “All sectors are behaving well. Growth is happening. Stress is at its lowest levels. As of now, there is no impact on our books... and we are watchful and mindful of it.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: China economy grows thanks to AI export boom but domestic slump remains a drag
articles.summary: China reported better-than-expected Q3 growth on Monday as robust exports of chips and electronics components on the back of a global artificial intelligence...
articles.body:
China reported better-than-expected Q3 growth on Monday as robust exports of chips and electronics components on the back of a global artificial intelligence boom buoy the world's second-largest economy, despite sluggish demand at home.

China's National Bureau of Statistics said the economy grew 4.5% from a year earlier in the quarter ending September, a slight improvement from the more than three-year low of 4.3% last quarter and meeting the lower end of Beijing's 4.5-5% annual target .

This came as China has demonstrated its resilience in weathering the economic shocks of President Donald Trump's tariff offensive – now on pause after both sides agreed to a truce – as well as the US's war with Iran, which has dragged down growth in other nations.

For the first nine months of 2026, the economy expanded 4.6%.

The latest quarterly figure underscores the continuing challenge facing China's leadership: the deepening imbalance that has made the country increasingly reliant on manufacturing and overseas markets.

The phenomenon has come to be described by economists as a "two-speed economy": a thriving export engine powered by high-tech manufacturing, alongside weak investment and stagnant domestic consumption. A prolonged housing market downturn , now in its fifth year, remains a drag, as an estimated 70% of Chinese household wealth is tied up in property.

Property investment plunged 20.2% in the first three quarters of the year, indicating that the country's real estate woes persist.

Investment, a major pillar of the Chinese economy, was still weak, Monday's figures showed. Fixed-asset investment, which includes spending on infrastructure, factories and property, fell 7.2% in the first nine months of the year from the same period in 2025, declining at the same pace as the first eight months, according to data released on Monday.

However, retail sales, a key gauge of consumption, saw a remarkable turnaround, growing 1.1% in September, an improvement from the modest 0.4% increase in August and the fastest growth since March.

"The economy moved forward under pressure and developed in a newer and better direction, with an increase in positive changes in key indicators," said Mao Shengyong, vice-minister of the National Bureau of Statistics, at a Monday press conference.

"At the same time, we must also recognize that the international environment is complex and volatile, the problem of insufficient domestic demand remains relatively prominent, and the foundation for the steady and positive growth of the economy still needs to be consolidated," he added.
